Zerubbabel, son of Shealtiel, is a figure from the Old Testament who led the Jews back from Babylon around 520 BC and rebuilt the temple. However, there is a difference in the texts above Shealtiel and below Zerubbabel. Matthew's account agrees with the Septuagint text, which lists Shealtiel as Zerubbabel's father, while the Masoretic text substitutes Shealtiel's brother Pedaiah. Some scholars suggest that Pedaiah may have fathered a son for Shealtiel through a levirate marriage, but most now accept the Septuagint reading as original.

Moving on to the second passage, the Delhi Metro's Phase 1 has 40 operational stations along two lines, with 22 underground stations. In the underground sections, a walkway runs along the length with cross passages every 250 metres for maintenance and emergency evacuation. The underground stations have an average width of 200 metres and an average depth of 20 feet from the ground level. The length of the stations in the Phase 1 extension is 180 metres. The elevated stations have three levels, while the underground stations have two. The stations are air-conditioned, disabled and elderly friendly, and equipped with an automatic fare collection system, announcement system, electronic display boards, escalators, lifts, and paid parking facilities for two and four wheelers in select stations.

In the Old Testament, Zerubbabel was a hero who led the Jews back from Babylon about 520 BC, governed Judah, and rebuilt the temple. Several times he is called a son of Shealtiel. He appears once in the genealogies in the Book of Chronicles, where his descendants are traced for several generations, but the passage has a number of difficulties. While the Septuagint text here gives his father as Shealtiel, the Masoretic text instead substitutes Shealtiel's brother Pedaiah—both sons of King Jeconiah, according to the passage.
